current.text: He missed all of last season with a torn ACL. He is about 18 months removed from the injury and fully healthy.
He made his preseason debut and looked pretty good.
Experts expect few restrictions on his minutes. He could play about 33 minutes a night right away.
He is expected to sit back-to-backs, especially early in the season.
Dallas is short on ball handlers. He is the only established guard and is a projected starter.
He is the second option on offense behind Cooper Flagg.
A trade is possible during the season.
Dallas has the league-high 16 back-to-backs but a 4-4-4 schedule in the fantasy playoffs, probably the best in the league.
If he keeps sitting back-to-backs, his playoff schedule could drop to about 10 games.
Dallas has a two-game week in the matchup starting March 1.
Experts project him as a top 15 to top 20 player per game.
Experts now take him around picks 30 to 38, in round 3. Pick 30 is the earliest Josh would take him.
Experts think the market overrates his risk. Among Kyrie, LeBron and Michael Porter Jr., he probably carries the fewest risks.
He is the best fantasy target on Dallas.
Dallas has no reason to tank, so a late-season shutdown is unlikely.

durable.text: He has a long history of knee injuries, including a torn ACL. He will not play 82 games.
He is 34, and his age adds risk to his health and minutes.
His category line has no weak category. His strongest categories are FT%, points and threes.

note: Experts now take him in round 3, around picks 30 to 38, and project top 15 to 20 per game. On Yahoo and ESPN he goes for about 12 USD, so his Yahoo value of 24 USD is a fair ceiling, and he was not drafted in our league last season. He has no weak category, so he fits any build and adds FT%, points and threes. Early in the season, check how often he sits back-to-backs (Dallas has 16, the most in the league) and how many minutes he plays, since that decides how much of the 4-4-4 playoff schedule he actually plays.
